name: Fomr
tagline: Visual form builder with unlimited responses, design controls, sharing, and embeds

pricing.notes: The live pricing page lists Pro at $17/month during a limited 50% offer, reduced from $34/month.
pricing.freeTier: The Free plan includes unlimited forms, responses, and team members, plus core design, publishing, and notification features.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms, responses and team members; 100MB storage; 1 workflow per form

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms, responses, team members and workflows; 10GB storage; custom domain and branding removal
tiers.notes: The displayed $17/month is a limited 50%-off offer; the page shows a regular price of $34/month. Exact yearly checkout price is not exposed.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms, responses and team members; 100GB storage; multiple custom domains; role management, audit trail and priority support
tiers.notes: Marked 'Coming soon' and not currently purchasable.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited forms, responses and team members; 100MB storage; 1 workflow per form
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + yearly advertised as 2 months free; exact yearly totals are not publicly exposed; 7-day money-back guarantee, no trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: The Pro price is a time-limited 50% promotion and may return to $34/month without a published end date; the $84/month Business tier is advertised but not yet buyable.

verdictSummary: A useful single-owner form builder is a realistic weekend project. Matching Fomr's visual editor, design depth, managed delivery, collaboration, integrations, and confidence that every public submission arrives turns it into an ongoing product rather than a one-shot clone.
coreLoopDIY: Create a single-owner form builder with live preview, publishable links, response storage, email notifications, and CSV export.
requirements: SMTP credentials in .env for optional notifications
whatYouLose: managed uptime, backups, and abuse controls
moatNotes: visual editor polish, dependable collection, and maintained integrations
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay to publish polished forms without operating a public data-collection service, maintaining email and spreadsheet integrations, or worrying about backups, spam, browser quirks, and lost responses.

priorArt.name: HeyForm
priorArt.desc: Open-source form builder with public forms, logic, and response collection.

alternatives.name: HeyForm
alternatives.desc: Typeform-style visual forms without the rent; one container to own the whole thing

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with MongoDB and KeyDB/Redis
facts.engines: Optional OpenAI-compatible API for AI features; default model documented as gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in HeyForm Cloud; self-hosted forms and responses live in MongoDB, cache/session data in KeyDB/Redis, and uploads on the server or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: HeyForm offers a visual form builder and unlimited self-hosted responses, but its design polish and hosting simplicity are weaker once you leave the hosted service and run MongoDB plus KeyDB yourself.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, a domain, reverse proxy/TLS, email configuration, and persistent database/storage volumes.

alternatives.name: Tally
alternatives.desc: A generous hosted form builder with logic and unlimited responses; branding is the upsell

facts.engines: Tally AI is available, but its underlying model provider is not publicly documented
facts.dataFormat: Forms and responses live in Tally's EU-hosted cloud; responses can be downloaded as CSV or synchronized to Google Sheets or Notion.
facts.gapVsPaid: Tally installs cleanly and permits unlimited free responses, but removing Tally branding, using a custom domain, and deeper visual customization require a paid plan.

alternatives.name: OpnForm
alternatives.desc: Open-source forms with unlimited respondents; the free self-hosted builder team stops at two

facts.install: Hosted signup, or the production Docker deployment
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in OpnForm Cloud; self-hosted forms and submissions live in MySQL or PostgreSQL, with uploaded files on configured local or object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpnForm gives you open-source forms and self-hosted responses, but the free self-hosted workspace is limited to two users and its design controls are less polished than Fomr's.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, a database, a public domain/TLS and mail/storage configuration; the free self-hosted edition allows two workspace users.

notes: The unusually capable free plan makes building a replacement less urgent than the verdict suggests.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal form builder inspired by Fomr, starting from an empty repository.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 16, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, and Drizzle ORM.
The core loop is create a form, preview it, publish it, collect responses, and export them.
Make it single-owner and protect the admin area with an ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env.
Create an admin form editor with a reorderable field list and a live respondent preview.
Support short text, long text, email, number, select, radio, checkbox, rating, date, and content blocks.
Allow required fields, labels, help text, placeholders, choices, and basic min/max validation.
Support one simple conditional rule per field: show it when another answer equals a configured value.
Add form-level colors, font choices, logo upload, cover image, spacing, and light or dark appearance.
Publish each form at /s/<slug> with accessible labels, keyboard navigation, and mobile layouts.
Validate every submission on the server against the saved form schema.
Store forms, immutable schema versions, responses, and timestamps in SQLite.
Provide a private response table with search, detail view, deletion, and CSV export.
Send optional owner notifications through SMTP, but keep collection working when SMTP is absent.
Add a honeypot, per-IP rate limiting, request-size limits, and safe upload handling for branding assets.
Include a configurable thank-you message and optional redirect URL.
Handle empty, loading, validation, success, not-found, and recoverable failure states.
Keep user data local and add JSON export and import for forms.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, billing, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret in .env and include a complete .env.example.
Write unit tests for schema validation and branching plus one end-to-end publish-and-submit test.
Create a README covering setup, deployment, data location, backups, SMTP, security limits, and recovery.
Deliberately exclude custom domains, team collaboration, OAuth integrations, payments, and enterprise compliance.
Deliberately exclude a marketplace-sized template library and promise only personal-scale reliability.
Run tests and a production build before finishing, fixing failures instead of merely describing them.
